youtube.baslik: Case: Present OAEs, Absent ABR (Auditory Neuropathy) | Lesson 288 | AIHEAR Audiology Academy
youtube.aciklama:
We interpret the findings of auditory neuropathy spectrum disorder in a fictional preterm infant case: the conflict between AABR and OAE results, the risk history, 1000 Hz tympanometry and the acoustic reflex, click ABR in two polarities with the cochlear microphonic, the tube-clamped control, and follow-up with VRA and aided cortical potentials.

AIHEAR Audiology Academy makes short, clear lessons for audiology students and professionals.

Sources: Joint Committee on Infant Hearing, Year 2019 Position Statement; Guidelines for Identification and Management of Infants and Young Children with Auditory Neuropathy Spectrum Disorder (Como, 2008); Hall, eHandbook of Auditory Evoked Responses; Katz, Handbook of Clinical Audiology.

This video is for educational purposes and does not replace diagnosis or treatment.

sahneler.alt: Cochlear microphonic, risk history and cortical follow-up
cumleler: Hello, and welcome to the AIHEAR Audiology Academy.
In this lesson we interpret, step by step, the findings of an infant with otoacoustic emissions but no auditory brainstem response.
Together we will apply the cochlear microphonic and polarity reversal, the risk history, and follow-up with cortical potentials.

maddeler.metin: NICU AABR: referred in both ears

cumleler: Our case is entirely fictional: a low birth weight infant born at thirty weeks of gestation.
The infant spent seven weeks in the neonatal intensive care unit and briefly needed respiratory support in the first days.
Severe jaundice developed in the intensive care unit and an exchange transfusion was needed.

cumleler.yazi: Before discharge, the infant was screened with automated auditory brainstem response, or AABR, and referred in both ears.
cumleler.ses: Before discharge, the infant was screened with automated auditory brainstem response, or A A B R, and referred in both ears.

cumleler: The family says the baby was later tested elsewhere with otoacoustic emissions, or OAE, and passed.
The infant is now one month of corrected age and has been brought in for a diagnostic evaluation.

cumleler.yazi: Asking about the risk history systematically is the first step in interpreting the findings; a NICU stay over five days is a key indicator.
cumleler.ses: Asking about the risk history systematically is the first step in interpreting the findings; a nick you stay over five days is a key indicator.

cumleler: Prematurity and low birth weight are among the known risk factors for auditory neuropathy.
Hyperbilirubinemia, or severe jaundice, needing exchange transfusion can damage especially the neural parts of the auditory pathway.
Lack of oxygen at or after birth, or hypoxia, is also asked about.

cumleler.yazi: Family history is asked too; genes such as OTOF can cause this picture even in infants with no risk factors.
cumleler.ses: Family history is asked too; genes such as O T O F can cause this picture even in infants with no risk factors.

cumleler: First, let us explain the conflict between the screening results.
The OAE reflects the function of the ear canal, the middle ear and the outer hair cells in the cochlea.

cumleler.yazi: The AABR also covers the inner hair cell, the auditory nerve and the brainstem pathway.
cumleler.ses: The A A B R also covers the inner hair cell, the auditory nerve and the brainstem pathway.

cumleler.yazi: If the problem lies beyond the outer hair cells, at the synapse or in the nerve, the OAE passes and the AABR refers.
cumleler.ses: If the problem lies beyond the outer hair cells, at the synapse or in the nerve, the OAE passes and the A A B R refers.

cumleler.yazi: This is why NICU infants staying over five days are screened with AABR; counting an AABR refer as a pass by OAE is not recommended.
cumleler.ses: This is why nick you infants staying over five days are screened with A A B R; counting an A A B R refer as a pass by OAE is not recommended.

cumleler: In the diagnostic evaluation, the middle ear is measured with a one thousand hertz probe tone.
Both ears show a clear positive peak rising above the baseline; middle ear function appears normal.
The acoustic reflex is tested with the same probe tone, but it cannot be obtained in either ear, even at the highest level.
An absent reflex despite a normal tympanogram calls for attention to hearing loss or a neural pathway problem.
A normal middle ear lets us interpret the OAE result in the next test with confidence.
Distortion product OAEs are clearly above the noise floor at most of the tested frequencies in both ears.
This finding shows that the outer hair cells in the cochlea are most likely working.
But the OAE does not assess the auditory nerve, and it does not tell us how much the infant hears.
The family heard this result earlier as good news, so the importance of the next test now needs to be explained.
A reduction of the emission with noise in the opposite ear, called contralateral suppression, is usually absent in auditory neuropathy.

cumleler.yazi: During natural sleep, a click auditory brainstem response, or ABR, is recorded at eighty five decibels nHL with insert earphones.
cumleler.ses: During natural sleep, a click auditory brainstem response, or ABR, is recorded at eighty five decibels n H L with insert earphones.

cumleler: The navy line shows the condensation polarity recording: there are regular oscillations in the first milliseconds.
The red line is rarefaction polarity: the same oscillations, this time in exactly the opposite direction.

cumleler.yazi: A response that follows the stimulus waveform and reverses with polarity is the hallmark of the cochlear microphonic, or CM.
cumleler.ses: A response that follows the stimulus waveform and reverses with polarity is the hallmark of the cochlear microphonic, or C M.

cumleler: After the oscillations die out, there is no repeatable wave in the region where wave V is expected.
Neural waves do not reverse with polarity; here, no non-reversing wave remains.

cumleler.yazi: The picture is the same in both ears: a large CM lasting a few milliseconds, and no neural ABR waves.
cumleler.ses: The picture is the same in both ears: a large C M lasting a few milliseconds, and no neural ABR waves.

cumleler: Stimulus artifact also reverses with polarity, so we must confirm that what we see really comes from the ear.
With insert earphones, sound reaches the ear with a delay of just under one millisecond; the response should start after this delay.
As a control, one more recording is made with the sound tube clamped, which keeps the sound from reaching the ear.
The dashed gray line is this control recording: the oscillations disappear completely.
A response that disappears when sound does not reach the ear is the cochlear microphonic; an electrical artifact would remain.
The middle ear is normal, but the acoustic reflex is absent.
The OAE and the cochlear microphonic are present, so the outer hair cells are working.
The click ABR shows no neural waves, even at high intensity.
This combination of findings is consistent with auditory neuropathy spectrum disorder, or ANSD.
Diagnosis and the search for a cause are carried out with the physician and the team; the audiologist reports the findings clearly.
The most important conclusion: in this infant, the ABR cannot be used to estimate hearing thresholds.

maddeler.metin: Explain the result in plain words

cumleler: In plain words, the family is told that the inner ear responds to sound, but sound is not carried in an orderly way along the nerve.
It is said honestly that, at this stage, we do not know how much the infant hears; no exact degree or promise is given.
For a family who received a pass earlier, this news is surprising; room is left for emotion, and questions are welcomed.
Then a concrete plan is discussed: physician review, repeat tests, and when behavioral tests will be done.
At the end of the meeting, a short written note with the main messages and a way to reach the clinic is given.
The infant is referred, with the findings, for evaluation by ENT and child neurology.
An absent or very thin auditory nerve gives similar findings; the physician may investigate this with magnetic resonance imaging.
Genetic evaluation may reveal causes such as the otoferlin gene; this may later affect what to expect from intervention.
Developmental and neurological follow-up is also part of the plan.

sahneler.metin: In an infant with a NICU history, an OAE pass does not rule out ANSD. Always add ABR in two polarities to the battery.
cumleler: A clinical tip: an infant holding an OAE pass result does not rule out auditory neuropathy.

cumleler.yazi: Especially with a history of NICU stay, prematurity or severe jaundice, always add ABR in two polarities to the battery.
cumleler.ses: Especially with a history of nick you stay, prematurity or severe jaundice, always add ABR in two polarities to the battery.

cumleler.yazi: In a recording made in a single polarity, a large CM can be mistaken for a neural wave.
cumleler.ses: In a recording made in a single polarity, a large C M can be mistaken for a neural wave.

cumleler: Inspect the polarities separately and add the tube-clamped control to your recording.
In some infants with jaundice, findings may improve over time, so in our case the ABR is repeated at three months corrected age.
The repeat recording does not change the picture; this is why no lasting conclusion should rest on a single recording.

cumleler.yazi: When the infant is developmentally ready, behavioral thresholds are obtained with visual reinforcement audiometry, or VRA.
cumleler.ses: When the infant is developmentally ready, behavioral thresholds are obtained with visual reinforcement audiometry, or V R A.

cumleler.yazi: Cortical auditory evoked potentials, or CAEP, show whether sound reaches the cortex.
cumleler.ses: Cortical auditory evoked potentials, or C A E P, show whether sound reaches the cortex.

cumleler: Intervention rests on behavioral thresholds and functional observations, not on the ABR; a device is fitted as a closely monitored trial.
Language and listening development are tracked at every visit with parent questionnaires and observation.

cumleler.yazi: At eight months corrected age, the infant is tested with VRA using insert earphones.
cumleler.ses: At eight months corrected age, the infant is tested with V R A using insert earphones.

cumleler: In the right ear, minimum response levels are between forty five and fifty five decibels HL.
In the left ear, the infant responds between fifty and fifty five decibels HL.
This result shows that, despite a completely absent ABR, the infant's thresholds are at the level of a moderate loss.
Because thresholds can fluctuate over time in auditory neuropathy, these values are confirmed again in later sessions.
The family is told that the infant's real difficulty may lie more in discriminating speech than in thresholds.

sahneler.baslik: Cortical response: does sound reach the *cortex*?
cumleler: After the device trial begins, an aided cortical test is done; the infant is awake and calm.
The dashed gray line is the unaided recording to a speech sound at moderate intensity: there is no clear response.
The blue line is the aided recording to the same sound: there is a clear positive wave.
At this age the P1 wave is later than in adults; here it appears at about two hundred thirty milliseconds.
The presence of a response is strong evidence that this speech sound reaches the cortex with the device.
An absent response alone does not prove that sound is not heard; the result is read together with observations and questionnaires.
In the device trial, the goal is not threshold gain so much as more functional responses to sounds and speech.
Because understanding in noise can be very poor in auditory neuropathy, remote microphone systems are a common later support.
Language and communication options are presented to the family neutrally; the decision belongs to the family.
If progress is not adequate, a cochlear implant evaluation may be considered; the team decides on an individual basis.

cumleler.yazi: In Türkiye, reimbursement rules (SUT) in auditory neuropathy require documented lack of benefit from at least six months of therapy.
cumleler.ses: In Türkiye, reimbursement rules, or S U T, in auditory neuropathy require documented lack of benefit from at least six months of therapy.

maddeler.metin: Click ABR: CM present, no waves

cumleler: Example report language: DPOAEs were present above the noise floor at most tested frequencies in both ears.

cumleler.yazi: Click ABR was recorded at eighty five decibels nHL in two polarities; a reversing cochlear microphonic is present, with no neural waves.
cumleler.ses: Click ABR was recorded at eighty five decibels n H L in two polarities; a reversing cochlear microphonic is present, with no neural waves.

cumleler: In the control recording with the sound tube clamped, the response disappeared.
One thousand hertz tympanometry shows a positive peak in both ears; acoustic reflexes were absent.

cumleler.yazi: Findings are consistent with ANSD; physician review and follow-up with repeat ABR, VRA and cortical testing are recommended.
cumleler.ses: Findings are consistent with ANSD; physician review and follow-up with repeat ABR, V R A and cortical testing are recommended.

maddeler.metin: OAE and CM present, no ABR: ANSD
Two polarities and tube control needed
Decide with behavioral thresholds and CAEP

cumleler: Absent ABR with present OAEs and cochlear microphonic is consistent with auditory neuropathy spectrum disorder.
The cochlear microphonic is recognized by reversing with polarity; the tube control separates it from stimulus artifact.

cumleler.yazi: NICU stay, prematurity, severe jaundice, hypoxia and family history are asked about systematically.
cumleler.ses: nick you stay, prematurity, severe jaundice, hypoxia and family history are asked about systematically.

cumleler: Because the ABR does not give thresholds, intervention rests on behavioral thresholds, cortical responses and functional observations.

sahneler.soru: Which response reverses with polarity and disappears when the tube is clamped?
sahneler.aciklama: Disappearing with the tube clamped shows the response comes _from the ear_.

cumleler.yazi: Test yourself: which response reverses when polarity changes and disappears when the sound tube is clamped?

cumleler: The correct answer is B: the cochlear microphonic.
Stimulus artifact also reverses, but it does not disappear when sound fails to reach the ear; neural wave V does not reverse with polarity.
